Based on the provided context, banks reported the impact of the FDIC special assessment as follows:

*   **Citigroup (Q4 2023):** Reported an FDIC special assessment of approximately $1.7 billion related to regional bank failures in March, which impacted expenses in "all other."
*   **Wells Fargo (Q1 2024):** Included $284 million ($0.06 per share) for the FDIC special assessment in its first-quarter results. This amount reflected recent updates from the FDIC regarding potential recoveries and was an addition to the $1.9 billion recorded in the prior quarter.
*   **Wells Fargo (Q2 2024):** Reported that it did not anticipate the $336 million of expense for the FDIC special assessment incurred during the first half of the year, which was subsequently included in its updated full-year non-interest expense guidance.
*   **PNC Financial Services (Q1 2024):** Recorded a pre-tax, non-core, non-interest expense of $130 million ($103 million after tax) related to the increased FDIC special assessment. This amount was included in total non-interest expenses and excluded from core non-interest expense calculations.
*   **Bank of America (Q4 2024 context referencing Q4 2023):** Noted that reported expenses were down year-over-year primarily because the fourth quarter of 2023 included an FDIC special assessment, which was treated as a notable item excluded from core expense comparisons.
